source: RFC 0007 §10.2 (maintainer review of 2026-11-21, R3-1: the service listener was a bare second Netty server)
statement: The control API's service port (`cosec.control.http.service-port`, `CTL-58`) is the application's own server on another port, not a second server of its own: it is built from a fresh server factory that Spring Boot's customizers have configured as they configure the application's (`server.ssl.*` with client authentication, `server.address`, HTTP/2, header and body limits, timeouts, forwarded-header handling, `server.netty.*`, the application's Netty server customizers and shared event loop), then given its port, and takes no property of its own. A host that makes `only-trusted-callers-can-reach` true by mutual TLS on the application's port serves the service port with mutual TLS: a request in clear text, or a client with no certificate, fails there as on the application port; one bound to an address binds the service port there and is not reachable on another. The application's own factory is read, never changed. Netty route providers of the application's server are not carried over: the service port serves the control API's service profile and nothing else. It stops as before: unbinding, the requests in flight within the grace, every connection still open closed.
guards: spring-boot:ControlServicePortSettingsTest#the service port of a running application closes an idle keep-alive connection when the application stops
spring-boot:ControlServicePortSettingsTest#with mutual TLS on the application port the service port is TLS with a client certificate too
spring-boot:ControlServicePortSettingsTest#with a bind address on the application port the service port listens there only
